title: I get the gta 6 hype but…
author: Brewgazer
selftext:
Okay I know still a whole lot of work to be done and no I’m not setting out to make a gta clone I was just simply experimenting yesterday trying to get clothes and hair to react to physics. I remember people being over the moon about the hair physics in gta and how they make it look like each hair moves like real hair… so I tried to embark on making it and also getting it to run well on a 3060 since people reviewing the trailer made it seem like that’s why you need a new play station to be able to see hair movement. I think I achieved it or pretty damn close, need to get hair to not mesh into the clothes and body, also need to get hair styles into the selection menu.

Don’t really know what I’m building but I was gonna add a bot to fight tonight… maybe we make this a comment it and I’ll add it type of thing.

If you want to pick my brain or if you have knowledge worth passing my way hmu

Edit: I used Claude connected to godot and blender. Model made in blender clothes made in blender, physics in godot, animations I told Claude to look for free mocap animations for fighting and no sign up to download and add to the character. Claude rigged it, as well. Pretty impressed need to fix the face a bit

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body: You probably want a simplified collision shape for the clothes so the hair doesn't clip through it constantly.

replies.author: Recoil42
replies.body:
>if you have any experience in getting the results

None of us do. That's why what GTA VI is doing is so impressive.

Realistic hair simulation in a full-fidelity game is extremely difficult to get right and an active area of research in the field of computer graphics. Hundreds of thousands of hairs must bend, twist, stretch, rub against other hairs, and cast shadows. Hair clumps together, separates, and tangles... it interacts with clothing and the human body — both of those already having their own really complicated physical systems — and getting all of that running in real-time is balls-to-the-wall difficult.

The TLDR of it all is that you're running into [this old XKCD comic](https://xkcd.com/1425/):

https://i.redd.it/yw7d0s206m0i1.png

You're going to find out just how hard all of this gets the moment you try to *"get hair to not mesh into the clothes and body"*, which is where you're at now.

replies.author: Brewgazer
replies.body: Well I’m ambitious and wanna figure it out and open source it. Think about how cool it would be if you could get a haircut in a game and see hair get cut like real life. Idk things could be really cool

replies.author: Recoil42
replies.body:
>Think about how cool it would be if you could get a haircut in a game and see hair get cut like real life.

I mean yeah; it would be really cool. If you want to achieve that be prepared to make it your entire career. There will have been an entire team of people at Rockstar working on hair alone for GTA VI — just that one thing. It's **that** complicated.
